before: 要不是生活所逼，他也不会一个人跑到外地打工。
after: 要不是被生活所逼，他也不会一个人跑到外地打工。
why: "生活所逼" needs the passive 被/为 frame; "被生活所逼" is the idiomatic form.

before: 过马路时看到黄灯，最好停下来等一等。
after: 开车遇到黄灯时，最好慢慢停下来，别抢着过去。
why: Pedestrians crossing the road face red/green signals, not a yellow light; reset the scene to driving.

before: When you see a yellow light while crossing the road, it's best to stop and wait.
after: When you meet a yellow light while driving, it's best to slow to a stop rather than rush through.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz sentence.

before: 把面粉和水搅在一起，就可以开始和面了。
after: 把面粉和水混在一起，揉成一个光滑的面团。
why: Original said "mix flour and water, then you can start 和面" — mixing them already is 和面, so the sentence was circular.

before: Mix the flour with water and you can start kneading the dough.
after: Mix the flour with water and knead it into a smooth dough.
why: Matches the rewritten example.

before: 多喝水能促进血液循环，对身体有好处。
after: 适当运动可以促进血液循环，对身体有好处。
why: Drinking water "promoting blood circulation" is a dubious claim; exercise is the standard collocation.

before: Drinking plenty of water improves blood circulation and is good for your health.
after: Moderate exercise improves blood circulation and is good for your health.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: 这两个城市之间的经济联系非常紧密。
after: 菜苗种得太密了，得拔掉一些才能长好。
why: Quiz tested 密 only inside 紧密; use the standalone adjective "dense" so the blank is the word itself.

before: The economic ties between these two cities are very close.
after: The seedlings were planted too densely; some need to be pulled out for the rest to grow well.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: 我昨晚没睡好，今天脑子一片空白，什么都想不起来。
after: 我这脑子真不好使，刚说过的话转眼就忘了。
why: "脑子一片空白" also works with the likely distractor 头脑 ("头脑一片空白"); "脑子不好使" is specific to 脑子.

before: I didn't sleep well last night, and today my mind is a total blank; I can't remember anything.
after: My brain really isn't working well; I forget what I've just said in the blink of an eye.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: 出门前多检查一遍，以免落下什么东西。
after: 客气话就免了吧，咱们都是老朋友了。
why: Quiz tested 免 only inside 以免; use the standalone verb "dispense with" so the blank is the word itself.

before: Check again before you leave so you don't leave anything behind.
after: Let's skip the pleasantries; we're old friends.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: saluran siaga; hotline
after: saluran telepon khusus; hotline
why: "saluran siaga" means an emergency standby line; a service hotline is "saluran telepon khusus".

before: 这部电影的结尾设计得非常巧妙，让人意想不到。
after: 他这步棋走得真妙，一下子就扭转了局面。
why: Quiz tested 妙 only inside 巧妙 (and 巧 would also be a plausible fill); use the standalone adjective.

before: The ending of this film is very cleverly designed and catches you completely by surprise.
after: That was a brilliant move of his; it turned the game around at a stroke.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: 这条路上禁止货车通行，只能走小汽车。
after: 这条路上禁止货车通行，只有小汽车可以走。
why: "只能走小汽车" is ungrammatical (the road cannot "walk cars"); rephrased.

before: 冬天在不通风的房间里烧炭取暖，很容易一氧化碳中毒。
after: 冬天在不通风的房间里烧炭取暖，很容易发生一氧化碳中毒。
why: "很容易一氧化碳中毒" lacks a verb; "发生……中毒" is the standard collocation.

before: 这次活动在社会上产生了很好的正面影响。
after: 这次活动在社会上产生了很大的正面影响。
why: "很好的正面影响" is redundant (good + positive); "很大的正面影响" is the natural collocation.

before: This event had a very good, positive impact on society.
after: This event had a big positive impact on society.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: 这次作文比赛字数限八百字以内，超出的要扣分。
after: 这次作文比赛每篇限八百字以内，超出的要扣分。
why: "字数限八百字" repeats 字 awkwardly.

before: Entries for this essay contest are limited to 800 characters; anything over loses points.
after: In this essay contest each entry is limited to 800 characters; anything over loses points.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: bergantung; berlama-lama, tidak mau beranjak; jelek (dalam 'lumayan')
after: bergantung; bermalas-malasan, enggan beranjak; jelek (dalam ungkapan "tidak jelek")
why: "jelek (dalam 'lumayan')" was confusing; also "berlama-lama" did not capture lingering in bed.

before: 他的观点我并不完全赞同，但我尊重他。
after: 对于周末加班的提议，全组只有他一个人举手赞同。
why: Original "我并不完全赞同他的观点" works equally with the look-alike distractor 认同 (also in this batch); voting by show of hands fits only 赞同.

before: I don't fully agree with his views, but I respect him.
after: Of the whole team, he was the only one who raised his hand in favor of the proposal to work weekends.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.

before: to book; to reserve; to schedule
after: to schedule, to fix in advance; to book, to reserve
why: Standard 预定 means pre-arranged/scheduled (预订 is the strict "book"); gloss should cover the core sense.

before: memesan; mereservasi; menjadwalkan
after: menjadwalkan, menetapkan sebelumnya; memesan
why: Matches the corrected gloss.

before: 国庆节期间酒店很紧张，最好提前一个月预定房间。
after: 由于天气原因，飞机没能按预定时间起飞。
why: Booking quiz was equally answerable with the sound-alike 预订 (the dictionary-standard word for booking rooms); "预定时间" is unambiguous.

before: Hotels are scarce during the National Day holiday; it's best to book a room a month in advance.
after: Because of the weather, the plane couldn't take off at the scheduled time.
why: Matches the rewritten quiz.
